newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. arms chief thinks Iraq has "missile force".
newsitem.headline: U.N. arms chief thinks Iraq has "missile force".

text.p: Chief U.N. arms inspector Rolf Ekeus said he told the Security Council on Wednesday he believed Iraq still had "a significant number of operational missiles which could constitute a complete missile force."
While there was a "theoretical possibility" Iraq had destroyed those missiles secretly, it had not shown the scrapped rockets, he told reporters.

Ekeus briefed the council on a recent trip to Baghdad during which he was unable to get Iraq to permit the removal for analysis in the United States of missiles it had destroyed without U.N. supervision shortly after the 1991 Gulf War. The analysis would be to obtain a definitive accounting of any remaining rocket stocks.

He said he told the Security Council: "We believe that Iraq is still holding a significant number of operational missiles which could constitute a complete missile force, including all support equipment, rocket fuel, launchers and everything."
He said there was "a theoretical possibility that Iraq has destroyed these missiles secretly...But then I took it that Iraq should show us the destroyed missiles. So that is a concern we have."
Ekeus did not say how many missiles might still be in Iraq's possession. In the past he has spoken of between six and 16 that were unaccounted for.
